snapshot.capital_scaled: ₹50 lakh–2 crore for manufacturing, a dealer network and field support
snapshot.distribution_note: Farmers trust demonstrations and dealers; FPOs and government schemes help

tailwinds: Farm labour shortages push farmers toward machines and tools.
Government schemes subsidise farm machinery, drones and irrigation.
Farmer producer organisations buy for many members.
Low-cost sensors and IoT make smart farming affordable.
headwinds: Farmers have little cash and buy after harvest.
Products must survive rough use and weather.
Farmers trust what they see work, not ads.
Service in rural areas is hard.
angle_2026: Labour shortages and subsidies are pushing even small farmers toward machines. In 2026, agritech device businesses grow by building rugged, affordable products, demonstrating them in fields, and selling through FPOs, dealers and subsidy schemes.
cost_basis: Estimated for a small team developing one farm device and selling through dealers and FPOs, 2026 prices.

unit_economics.note: Sales peak before sowing and harvest. Plan production and cash around the crop calendar.

investor_probes: How much time or money does it save a farmer?
How do you service it in villages?
bootstrap_takeaway: Test the device with 10 farmers for a full season, then sell through FPOs and local dealers with field demonstrations.
sourcing_edge: Local fabrication workshops can make prototypes and small batches cheaply. Agricultural universities and KVKs help with testing and farmer introductions.
licences: Testing at government-approved centres for subsidy eligibility

hard_truths.title: Cash-poor buyers
hard_truths.text: Farmers buy after harvest. Offer credit through FPOs or financing partners.

hard_truths.title: Rough use
hard_truths.text: Devices must be rugged. Test in real conditions.

hard_truths.title: Trust
hard_truths.text: Farmers need to see it work. Demonstrate in fields.

hard_truths.title: Service
hard_truths.text: Rural service is hard. Train local mechanics.

plan_goal: The aim is 50 devices sold through FPOs or dealers, with positive farmer feedback.
